summary: Round 2, narrow. Both round-1 majors verified closed against the staged bytes. (1) Delivery's class javadoc no longer makes any of the three falsified claims: it scopes 'bytes in hand / no request' to inline and proxy, states that under direct segment() is empty and the consumer does fetch through SegmentSource, names the falsified sentences explicitly, and states the per-run rate with M5.45h owning the merge and ConsumerClient.decodeInto named as the coalescing point -- which is true, since decodeInto is the only caller of bytesOf and bytesOf is the only fetch site. (2) The measured survivor (hoisting the null-source check above the via check in ConsumerClient.bytesOf) now dies: theSEAMIsNOTUsedWhenViaIsNotDIRECT pushes an INLINE delivery to a client built WITH a source, so the swapped order reaches segmentSource.fetch(null) and ServesOneUrl.fetch NPEs on grant.url() before the first offset assertion, and source.asked is asserted empty. The three test additions disturb nothing already passed: the PROXY arm kills the via != DIRECT -> via == INLINE mutation that nothing else reached; the second delivery under SECOND_GRANT kills a client that memoizes the first grant or ignores the parameter (containsExactly pins both urls and their order) and does not change what the first delivery asserts. Cost lens re-checked on the final bytes: one fetch per DIRECT delivery, i.e. per run per segment, which this row is explicitly permitted to leave to M5.45h; no production SegmentSource exists, NodeSubscriptions still uses the three-argument ConsumerClient so a production direct delivery would hit the IllegalStateException rather than a GET, and criterion 6 holds. The only two binjava.binstore strings under client/src are javadoc, confirming criterion 3's claim. One minor recorded, not to be fixed in a third round.

findings.title: the javadoc's 'segment() is EMPTY under direct' is the one asymmetry the compact constructor does not refuse
findings.failure_scenario: The corrected javadoc states as fact that under `direct` {@link #segment()} is EMPTY, but the compact constructor (Delivery.java:69-80) guards only the two grant asymmetries: grant==null with DIRECT, and grant!=null with non-DIRECT. `new Delivery(key, seg, 1, 0L, FetchMode.DIRECT, realBytes, grant)` is accepted, and ConsumerClient.bytesOf (ConsumerClient.java:120-128) takes the DIRECT branch unconditionally, so those in-hand bytes are silently discarded and a whole-object GET is issued for bytes the process already held -- one needless consumer-side request per such delivery, invisible to the ingester's CountingBinStore for the reason this very javadoc gives. Unreachable today (SubscriptionHub's DIRECT push carries EMPTY and M1.11b ships no production transport), which is why this is minor and not major; but it is the same 'refused where it is BUILT' discipline the rest of this record applies, applied to two of the three combinations. Record it in the commit body or as a row for M5.45h, which is where a real transport and the merge arrive together.
